what_lilly_says: Lilly uses the tropical zodiac of 12 equal 30° signs measured from the vernal equinox.
what_the_app_does: The app reads each body by the IAU zodiac constellation on the ecliptic at its longitude (13 unequal bands, 1930 Delporte boundaries), and treats that constellation as the sign.

what_lilly_says: Terms and faces are degree ranges within a 30° sign (p.104).
what_the_app_does: Each range is stretched proportionally across the constellation's true width: a body 40% of the way through IAU Virgo is read as Virgo 12°. Exaltation degrees are rescaled the same way, for display only.

what_lilly_says: Lilly has no Ophiuchus; every ecliptic point lies in one of his 12 signs.
what_the_app_does: A body whose ecliptic band is Ophiuchus has no house ruler, exaltation, triplicity, term or face. It is scored as peregrine (-5), and the screen says why. A body whose real (RA/Dec) constellation is off the zodiac (e.g. Cetus) is flagged but still read by its ecliptic band.

what_lilly_says: p.113: a planet is under the Sun-beams until 17° from the Sun. Yet in his worked example (pp.178-180) Lilly gives Mercury (about 14.6° from the Sun) and the Moon (about 16°) "Free from Combustion" +5 and no "under the beams" -4.
what_the_app_does: Option "Sun-beams rule": "table" (default; the p.113/p.115 rule as written) or "Lilly's worked example" (only combustion within 8°30' is scored; otherwise +5).

what_lilly_says: Partile = "exactly so many degrees" as the aspect, illustrated with equal degree numbers in two signs (p.106).
what_the_app_does: Unequal IAU bands give no common degree numbering, so the app counts an aspect as partile when it is within 1° of exact.

what_lilly_says: Besieged = placed betwixt the bodies of Saturn and Mars; his example has all three in one sign (p.114).
what_the_app_does: The app counts a planet as besieged when it lies on the shorter arc between Saturn and Mars and that arc is 30° or less.

what_lilly_says: p.115 gives Regulus in 24 Leo, Spica in 18 Libra, Algol in 20 Taurus "or within five degrees". In his example Lilly uses 5° for Spica and Regulus too (p.179).
what_the_app_does: The app computes the stars' apparent positions for the chart date and uses a 5° orb in ecliptic longitude for all three.

what_lilly_says: p.107 gives two orb columns, his own and "according to others". He says he uses sometimes the one, sometimes the other.
what_the_app_does: Default = Lilly's first column (Saturn 10, Jupiter 12, Mars 7.5, Sun 17, Venus 8, Mercury 7, Moon 12.5). Option = the other column. Aspect orb = the sum of the two moieties (half-orbs), p.107/p.110.

what_lilly_says: p.65 prints the mean motion as "31 degr. 27 min."; on p.178 Lilly uses 31 min. 27 sec.
p.33: a planet within five degrees of a cusp has its virtue assigned to that house.
what_the_app_does: The app assigns a planet within 5° before the next cusp to that next house.

what_lilly_says: Lilly erects figures by the Tables of Regiomontanus (Book I ch. IV).
what_the_app_does: The app computes Regiomontanus cusps for the true latitude. The cusps are ecliptic longitudes, so they are independent of the zodiac frame.

what_lilly_says: The planet of the day rules the first hour from sunrise and the eighth (e.g. Saturn on Saturday, p.61; Jupiter on Thursday, p.65). The hours run in Chaldean order.
what_the_app_does: The app uses unequal hours: (sunset - sunrise)/12 by day and (next sunrise - sunset)/12 by night, at the chart location. With no sunrise (polar), it falls back to equal hours from local mean midnight and flags it.
status: sourced (method of hour length: standard unequal hours)

what_the_app_does: Uranus, Neptune and Pluto are drawn on the wheel but get no dignity, score, or Lilly reading.

what_lilly_says: Lilly judges horary questions and nativities with these tables.
what_the_app_does: The app reads a moment chart: it shows dignity scores and Lilly's descriptions. It is offered for study and reflection; controlled studies have not found astrological charts to be predictive.

what_lilly_says: In the worked example (pp.178-180) Lilly omits two items his p.115 table prescribes: the Sun in Leo by day gets no triplicity (+3), and Jupiter, 15.7° behind the Sun, gets no "Orientall" (+2). In his Book III nativity table he does stack dignities (Venus: own house 5 + own terms 2).
what_the_app_does: The app applies the p.115 table cumulatively. Validation against the example: 5 of 7 planets reproduce Lilly's totals exactly, and the other two differ only by these two items.

what_lilly_says: Lilly defines peregrine as having no essential dignity in that degree (p.112). He gives mutual reception the same points as house or exaltation (p.115).
what_the_app_does: The app does not also mark a planet peregrine when it is in mutual reception.

what_lilly_says: Lilly's ephemerides give the Dragon's Head; the method is not stated.
what_the_app_does: The app uses the mean lunar node (Meeus 47.7).

what_lilly_says: Triplicity rulers change by day and night.
what_the_app_does: A chart is diurnal when the Sun is above the horizon (altitude above -0.83°, i.e. between sunrise and sunset).
